reader.requirement: At --std 85 each literal-1/literal-2 (a nonnumeric literal or figurative constant) and each identifier-2/identifier-3 (an alphanumeric item, group or alphanumeric function, its full content) in the DELIMITED BY ... OR list is a delimiter the sender is examined against, with subscripts evaluated once before the examination (1985 substantive-change item 34), the earliest match winning and a tie going to the first listed (GR11, GR12).
reader.edition-search: grep -i 'edition|version|dialect|DialectLevel' over StringUnstringBinder.cs, StringEmitter.cs, CobolStringOps.cs, OperandText.cs, FigurativeConstants.cs; grep -i 'unstring|delimit' over ConstructRegistry.g.cs and VersionConformancePass.cs. The binder's ctx.Edition uses are BoundRejected.Report/BoundOperandError.Report (the diagnostic channel, fixed EditionSeverity.Error) and ctx.Edition.At (the diagnostic cursor); neither switches behaviour. The only UNSTRING construct gate is unstring-sender-reference-modified-2002 (the sender, not this rule).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: da4 covers only a function delimiter; literal OR lists with a same-position tie, an identifier delimiter with a trailing space, a group delimiter, a subscripted delimiter whose subscript a receiver stores, a figurative delimiter, and the refusals are not exercised

probes.expected: GR4/GR11/GR12: delimiters applied in the listed order ("," before ",," at one position, and the reverse); an identifier delimiter is its whole content "* "; a group delimiter "XY"; C(PTR) is evaluated once, so storing PTR=05 through BB leaves the delimiter "12" for E

probes.printed: COBOL1651 delimiter '3' is a numeric literal; 'DN' category numeric; 'DA' category alphabetic; 'ALL ","' begins with the word ALL
probes.expected: §1985:VI.6.27.3 SR1: nonnumeric literals, no ALL figurative; SR2: identifier-2 category alphanumeric

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR4  the text is in GR4 (quoted: "Literal-1 or the data item referenced by identifier-2 specifies a delimiter")
OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR12  the text is in GR12 (quoted: "No character(s) in the sending field can be considered a part of more than one delimiter")
OK  §1985:VI.6.27.3 SR1  the text is in SR1 (quoted: "must be nonnumeric literals")

reader.notes: DelimiterText renders the delimiter values once at initiation, over the places IdentifyOperands froze, and passes them as a string[] to UnstringExtract. Its earliest-match scan, with ties going to the first listed, follows GR12's order. A value is read again only when a receiver overlaps its storage, which GR21 leaves undefined. No edition arm on this path.
